subject: Vendr: bulk claim for existing Whistic proofs + Archer QnA stitch
messages:
From: Alex Harrington <alex.harrington@clearskyhealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: onboarding@vendr.com
Date: 2027-10-05T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Migrating Whistic proofs to Vendr + Archer QnA stitch

Hi Diego —

We just completed an internal decision to move our vendor profiles off Whistic and consolidate on Vendr. We have several evidence blobs already in S3 and a set of Whistic proofs we want to claim so we don’t have to re-upload everything. Two asks from my side:

1) Can Redwood’s onboarding team help with a bulk-claim flow so Vendr can assert proof possession against our existing S3 objects?
2) We also want Archer QnA fields to be mapped to the Vendr CAIQ taxonomy so our procurement team can keep using the Archer exports.

I attached a small manifest (clearsky_vendr-claim-manifest.csv) listing a sample of objects we’d like claimed. Happy to run through details in a short call.

Thanks —
Alex
Alex Harrington
Security Operations, ClearSky Health
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Harrington <alex.harrington@clearskyhealth.com>
Cc: onboarding@vendr.com, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-05T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Migrating Whistic proofs to Vendr + Archer QnA stitch

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the overview and the manifest. We can support a bulk-claim approach that minimizes re-uploads. Proposed plan:

- Step 1: Vendr issues a claim session URL (OIDC-backed) for ClearSky. Your S3 objects will be referenced in the CSV with object paths and a short integrity hash column.
- Step 2: ClearSky (you) generate presigned PUT URLs for the minimal handshake files or allow Vendr to validate via signed GET if you prefer read-only verification. We can accept either. See attached s3-presign-policy.txt with our suggested TTL and ACLs.
- Step 3: Vendr performs possession checks and creates CAIQ-aligned assertions.
- Step 4: We run an Archer field-mapping pass (draft mapping attached: caiaq-archer-fieldmap-v1.xlsx) to stitch QnA keys into your Archer exports so procurement sees the same coverage.

Open items:
- Do you want Redwood to host the small claim orchestration (we can run the presign generator under a short-term service account)?
- Who should be the Vendr service account email we whitelist for S3?

If that works I’ll coordinate a 30-min workshop with Vendr and Archer next week to walk the team through the CSV format, TTLs, and test claim.

Diego Fernandez
Senior Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Vendr Onboarding <onboarding@vendr.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Alex Harrington <alex.harrington@clearskyhealth.com>
Cc: Sasha Nguyen <sasha.nguyen@archercloud.com>
Date: 2027-10-06T10:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Migrating Whistic proofs to Vendr + Archer QnA stitch

Hi Alex + Diego —

We can absolutely support the bulk-claim flow. Quick details for the team:

- We’ll provide an OIDC claim session link (one-time) that your security admin will authenticate into.
- Required manifest columns: object_path, bucket, sha256_hash, claimed_on (ISO), preferred_ttl_hours. Your sample CSV looks fine; please ensure bucket names are correct.
- For possession checks we accept:
  * presigned GET (30m TTL) pointing to each object OR
  * presigned POST to upload a 256-byte claim marker (our default) — both are acceptable.

We also have a small Archer adapter that maps CAIQ comments -> Archer QnA rows. Sasha from Archer is copied to confirm connector requirements.

Next steps for onboarding:
1) Diego to share the Vendr claim-session URL with ClearSky.
2) ClearSky to confirm service account(s) and upload a 50-row sample CSV.
3) Vendr run a test pass and flag any mismatches.

—Vendr Onboarding Team
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-06T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vendr claim session — quick internal sync

Diego / Mina —

Thanks for looping me in. A couple quick notes from Security/Platform: 

- If Redwood will host the presign generator we should use a short-lived STS role with an auditable session name and rotate keys post-workshop.
- Mina: can you confirm whether we need to sign any of the CAIQ assertions with our KMS key (we typically avoid signing third-party possession claims but can provide a signed hash reference if ClearSky requests it).

Diego — I’ll be on the workshop but can you draft the access matrix (who can request presigns, who can approve claims) before the call?

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Platform Security, Redwood Inference
